text:
The "open-door notes" were the Open Door Notes (1899–1900), U.S. Secretary of State John Hay's diplomatic messages to major powers with interests in China, urging them to keep trade access to China open and respect Chinese territorial and administrative integrity. They aimed to prevent exclusive spheres of influence from shutting out American commerce. The note claiming they concerned Chinese immigration to the U.S. is incorrect.

CONFIDENCE: 95
